question.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+\,\,\frac{1}{4}$ $36t-42$ .
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 3{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-{e}^{-t}\cdot 3{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ -3{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =-[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ -3{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3t{e}^{2t} \\ 12t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-3t{e}^{2t} \\ 12t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -3t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 12t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=-3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-3\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -3t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =(-3t)\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (-3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t}+\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}t{e}^{2t}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t}(1-2t).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=12t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=12\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 12t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =12t\cdot {e}^{t}-\int 12\cdot {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =12t{e}^{t}-12{e}^{t} \\  & =12{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 3{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2t}(1-2t) \\ 12{e}^{t}(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}6(1-2t)+48(t-1) \\ 9(1-2t)+48(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}36t-42 \\ 30t-39\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
